BACKGROUND. The hosted @llm-canon test in scene-runtime.spec.js (title 'judges every reached scene against its committed knowledge canon @llm-canon') submits one scripted command per turn through `submitTurn(page, input)` from helpers.js and then asserts `expect(payload.state?.turn_index).toBe(turnIndex + 1)`. A staged run aborted at turn 46: the scripted 3A command 'Meet the imprisoned official and request the emergency gate authorization.' was ambiguous, so the engine answered with a clarification question ('Do you mean the emergency surface gates or the facility gate?') and consumed NO turn, so turn_index did not advance. The engine behaviour is by design. The server sets `payload.clarification = { original_command, noun, options: [{id, name}, ...], round }` on such a response (storygame/web_demo.py ~line 448; frontend/src/clarification.js shows the contract). The page itself attaches `clarifies`/`clarification_round` to the NEXT input the player types, so the harness answers a clarification simply by submitting the name of one option as the next input through the same submitTurn; the engine then resolves the original command and returns the real turn.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR. After a submitted scripted command the canon loop must answer any clarification and treat the FINAL (non-clarification) response as the turn. Implement it as a pure, injectable async helper in canon-policy.js: `answerClarifications({ payload, submit, maxRounds = 2 })` where `submit(inputText)` returns the next payload (the spec passes a closure calling `submitTurn(page, text)` and `resolveWarningIfPresent(page)` exactly like the first submit). While `payload.clarification` is present: take its first option, submit that option's `name` as the answer, and use the returned payload; stop when there is no clarification. If still clarifying after `maxRounds` answers, throw an Error whose message names the original command and noun (a clarification the script cannot resolve is a real harness failure, loudly). Return `{ payload, answers }` where answers is the array of option names submitted (empty when none). Validate with a clear Error if clarification.options is empty or the first option lacks a non-empty string name. Do not parse prose: only the typed payload.clarification field decides.

In the spec, call it right after the existing first `submitTurn` + `resolveWarningIfPresent` and use the returned payload for everything that follows. IMPORTANT: the package clock controller (frontend/e2e/package-clock-controller.js) disarms its armed milestone on the FIRST observed response, which would be the clarification response. Read that file (arm, turnsUntilMilestone, observeTurnResponse, history). Make sure the milestone is armed again before each clarification answer is submitted (inside the submit closure: if `milestone` is set, `controller.arm(milestone)` before submitting the answer) and that `timing` (the `controller.history().at(-1)` value) is taken from the FINAL response so overshoot detection and observed_timing describe the real turn. Keep `turnsUntilMilestone` computed once from the state before the scripted command. Keep the `expect(payload.state?.turn_index).toBe(turnIndex + 1)` assertion exactly as is; it now sees the resolved turn. Record the clarification answers on the progress row (add `clarification_answers: answers` only when non-empty) and keep `input` as the scripted command. The first-response payload may be returned unchanged when no clarification occurs: behaviour for ordinary turns must not change.

TESTS in canon-policy.test.js (node:test, assert/strict, hand-built payloads and a fake `submit`): no clarification -> payload returned untouched, submit never called, answers []; one clarification -> submits the first option name once and returns the second payload; two chained clarifications are both answered; still clarifying after maxRounds throws and the message contains the original command and the noun; empty options and a missing name throw; the submitted inputs are exactly the option names in order. Verify each expectation by running the tests. Style: match the surrounding files; no unrelated refactors.
